title: minimax-m3 : forward quant scales to the graph (fixes #31063)
body:
Fixes #31063

## Problem

`MiniMaxM3ForCausalLM` checkpoints ship NVFP4 routed experts and MXFP8 dense weights. The generic scale pass in `llama-model.cpp` correctly loads the resulting `.scale` tensors into `layer.ffn_{up,gate,down}_exps_s` (per-expert NVFP4 scale2), `layer.ffn_{up,gate,down}_s` (dense) and `layer.ffn_{up,gate,down}_shexp_s` (shared expert) — but `src/models/minimax-m3.cpp` never forwards any of them to the graph.

`build_moe_ffn()` defaults these parameters to `nullptr`, so `build_lora_mm_id()` never enters its `w_s` branch and the routed-expert weights are used as `q` instead of `q * block_scale * G`. With G ≈ 15123 for M3.1 Flash the MoE branch swamps the residual and output is token soup — matching the diagnosis in #31063.

## Fix

Forward all nine scale tensors at the three FFN call sites (dense lead, routed experts, shared expert), matching the pattern already used by `flint`, `deepseek32`, `qwen3moe` and the other NVFP4-capable MoE models. All are `TENSOR_NOT_REQUIRED` loads, so this is a no-op for checkpoints without scales.

Attention and nextn scale application is unchanged — `build_lora_mm` consumes `wq_s`-style scales generically (`llama-graph.cpp:1868`), so no changes are needed there.

## Verification

- Builds clean with MSVC (`build-msvc` Release), no new warnings.
- Code-level: the call sites now match the working reference implementations byte-for-byte in structure; previously the last positional argument was `il`, which silently bound `probs_in`/`gate_up_exps`/all scales to their `nullptr` defaults.
- Runtime verification needs the (not yet public) M3.1 Flash GGUF; the issue reporter's debugging (4-layer dense vs MoE divergence, G ≈ 15123) precisely matches this root cause, so I could not reproduce end-to-end locally — happy to iterate if reviewers want an additional guard (e.g. a warning when `*_exps_s` is non-null but the arch graph ignores it).

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — an AI coding assistant was used to analyze the codebase, implement the fix, and run the verification described above
